claims.claim: Cyril of Alexandria was Patriarch of Alexandria from 412 to 444.
Cyril of Alexandria was born c. 376 and died in 444.
The fragment mentions 'the opinion of Apollinarius and the blasphemy of Nestorius' in its opening lines.
The fragment references the faith confirmed by 'the blessed and saving symbol in Nicaea.'
The fragment states that the author has not attacked the pious but rather those who disturb the church and its Christ-loving people.
Cyril of Alexandria was involved in the Nestorian controversy, a dispute over Christological views that was decided at the First Council of Ephesus in 431.
The dispute between Cyril and Nestorius, Patriarch of Constantinople, led to churches supporting Nestorius' teachings splitting from the Orthodox church.
Cyril of Alexandria wrote multiple works against Nestorius, including the 'Five Tomes against Nestorius' and 'Scholia on the Incarnation of the Only-Begotten.'
Cyril of Alexandria was named a doctor of the church in 1882.
